question.text: The battles of Breteinfield and Lutzen took place during this major religious conflict, which lasted from 1618 to 1648.
question.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

swap.leadin: Also known as Henry Bolingbroke, this man became King of England after deposing Richard II in 1399.
swap.text: Identify this English king who was later succeeded by his son upon his 1413 death.
swap.clue: During his last days, his court was split between factions loyal to his successor and those loyal to Thomas Arundel, archbishop of Canterbury.

question.text: The title Emperor of the Romans would later morph into this position, holders of which were chosen by German Prince-Electors. Other holders of this title included Otto the Great and Frederick Barbarossa.
question.answerHtml: Holy Roman Emperor [accept German-Roman Emperor or Romanorum Imperator or Rex Romanorum; prompt on Emperor; do not accept or prompt on “Roman Emperor”]
question.clue: The Treaty of Pressburg invalidated this office after the battle of Austerlitz in 1806, and it was selected by seven electors after the 1356 Golden Bull.

swap.leadin: Identify some people in the history of a certain empire that was neither holy nor Roman.
swap.text: The "first German to be called emperor of Italy," this man solidified his power by defeating the Magyars at Lechfeld and the Obodrites at Recknitz and established the Holy Roman Empire.
swap.clue: He had earlier thwarted Berengar, the king of Burgundy, by venturing into Italy a year before his coronation and marrying Adelaide, though he was drawn back to his homeland to put down a revolt by the Duke of Lotharingia, Conrad.

question.leadin: This Czech priest was burned at the stake for heresy in 1415 at the Council of Constance.
question.text: Name this man, who denounced the sale of indulgences by Antipope John XXIII. During a set of wars named for this man, handheld firearms such as hand cannons were first extensively used.
question.clue: Prokop the Great led forces that pioneered the use of war wagons among this man's Taborite followers in a 15th-century conflict.

swap.leadin: This leader defeated the Seljuks at the Battle of Iconium before his death.
swap.text: Name this Holy Roman Emperor who tried to participate in the third crusade. While traveling to it, he drowned at the Saleph River due to his armor being too heavy.
swap.answerHtml: Frederick Barbarossa [or Frederick I or Friedrich I or Federico I; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: This man crossed the Saleph River to participate in a conflict he organized with Philip Augustus and Richard the Lionheart.

question.text: The king of this territory served as the third elector. Frederick the Winter King ruled this territory during the 30 Years War, and it was earlier ruled by King Wenceslas.
question.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Jan Zizka.
swap.text: Zizka was a military commander of this pre-Reformation Czech religious group in a series of their namesake "wars." They followed a man who was burned at the stake in 1415.
swap.clue: These people, led by Jan Zelivsky, threw Catholic magistrates out of a window during the First Defenestration of Prague.

question.text: The Guelphs grew out of the Lombard League, formed to resist this Holy Roman Emperor's influence in Italy. This emperor drowned in the Saleph River while leading the Third Crusade.
question.answerHtml: Frederick I [or Frederick Barbarossa; or Friedrich I; or Friedrich Barbarossa; prompt on Frederick; prompt on Freidrich]
question.clue: This man was forced to sign the Treaty of Venice following his defeat at the Battle of Legnano by the Lombard League.

swap.text: The third Holy Roman Emperor with this name was a close ally of the Piast king Boleslaw I. The first Holy Roman Emperor of this name, nicknamed "the Great," beat the Magyars at Lechfeld in 962.
swap.answerHtml: Otto [or Otto III; or Otto I; or Otto the Great]
swap.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

question.text: This confederation of electorates in the Holy Roman Empire fought for Lutheranism against Charles V before being routed at the Battle of Muhlberg.
question.clue: Taking its name from a town in Thuringia, this group was first formed by Philip I of Hesse and John Frederick I of Saxony.

swap.leadin: Six "Letters of Relation" were written to a ruler with this name by the conquistador Pedro de Valdivia during his conquest of modern Chile.
swap.text: Give this name of a Holy Roman Emperor and Spanish king whose extensive dominions included Naples, Burgundy, and much of the New World.
swap.answerHtml: Charles V [or Charles I of Spain; or Charles of Ghent; or Archduke of Austria Charles I; or Charles II, the Duke of Burgundy and Lord of the Netherlands; accept “Carlos” or “Karl” or “Karel” or “Carles” or“Carolus” in place of “Charles”]
swap.clue: He signed the Peace of Augsburg with the Schmalkaldic League and during the Italian Wars captured Francis I at the Battle of Pavia.

question.text: This first king of the Ottonian dynasty gets his nickname from the legend that he was fixing birding nets when told that he had been elected King of Germany.
question.clue: His wife accompanied him on his campaigns building monasteries, one of which was their burial site of Quedlinburg.

swap.leadin: Its chapel has a famous octagonal dome and its hot sulphur springs made it a popular nineteenth-century spa resort.
swap.text: Name this city that was the namesake of treaties ending the War of Devolution and the War of Austrian Succession. It was also the capital of the Carolingian empire of Charlemagne.
swap.clue: Ravenna's San Vitale was probably the model for this city's Palatine Chapel.

question.leadin: The losing side of this battle planned to recycle the strategy of fory-five years earlier, when they had defeated Louis the Child at the same site.
question.text: Identify this 955 battle at which the Magyar advance westward was decisively stopped.
question.clue: At the onset of this battle, the brother-in-law of the winning commander returned from exile to fight in this conflict.

swap.leadin: In this battle, an unauthorized charge initiated by Pappenheim instantly routed the Saxons under Elector John George I.
swap.text: Name this pivotal 1631 battle in which more mobile Swedish troops outflanked and crushed the traditionally arranged imperials under Tilly.
swap.clue: Another cavalry charge by Furstenberg drove off John George I and his Saxon troops, exposing the eventual victor's left flank.

question.leadin: Name these battles of the Thirty Years War.
question.text: Two cousins named Ferdinand inflicted a crushing blow on the Swedish army at this 1634 battle, in which the Spanish tercios made up for their poor showing at Breitenfeld.
question.clue: This 1634 battle crushed the momentum of Protestant forces under Swedish leadership. In this battle, Habsburg forces under Ferdinand III and the Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand defeated the League of Heilbronn and captured Gustav Horn.

swap.text: Much of the Hussites' military success under Zizka stemmed from his pioneering of this tactic, in which bow and pistol-armed soldiers would hide in the namesake vehicles, and then charge once enemy cavalry faltered.
swap.answerHtml: the Wagenburg [or wagon fort; accept the Tabor or Laager; do not accept the specifically Russian “gulai-gorod”; prompt on descriptions like “they tied wagons together"]

question.text: This Bohemian king, the son of Holy Roman Emperor Henry VII and Margaret of Brabant, died fighting at the Battle of Crecy despite being blind. He shares his royal name with an English ruler called "Lackland."

swap.leadin: Name some people and things with related -isms.
swap.text: This man discussed a Bethlehem Steel Company worker named Schmidt who was "like an ox" in his diatribe against rules of thumb in factories, The Principles of Scientific Management, a discipline that is sometimes called this man's -ism.
swap.clue: A ruler of this name was a cousin of Henry the Lion who abandoned his support for Antipope Calixtus III after failing to take the fort of Alessandria, which was named for his enemy, Pope Alexander III.
